newsitem.title: USA: 1996 was the year in music for Alanis Morissette.
newsitem.headline: 1996 was the year in music for Alanis Morissette.

text.p: 1996 was the year in music dominated by Alanis Morissette, whose "Jagged Little Pill" was the best-selling debut by a female artist in American music history, a music trade group said on Monday.

The album, which featured darkly introspective lyrics and an original sound, sold 10 million units this year, adding to 4 million sold in 1995, the Recording Industry Association of America said in its year-end sales totals.

That surpassed 12 million units sold of Whitney Houston's self-titled debut, the RIAA said, and put Morissette, a Canadian, on a pace to break Boston's record of 15 million units with its self-titled debut album released in 1976.
Morissette's Grammy-winning album sold nearly 1 million units a month and was near the top of the charts all year.

Second on the list of best sellers was the Beatles' "Anthology, Volume I," with 8 million sold in 1996. The first in a three-part series of previously unreleased material, the double-disc album sold 4 million copies but the RIAA said it doubles the figures under its multi-disc category.
"The Beatles Anthology, Volume 2" sold over 3 million units and two singles, "Free As a Bird" and "Real Love," reached gold status with sales of more than 500,000 each.
Artists who sold 7 million copies in 1996 also included Morissette's fellow Canadian Celine Dion's "Falling Into You" and the all-female artist soundtrack to the movie "Waiting to Exhale."
It was Dion's best-selling album so far and it spawned two platinum singles.

The "Waiting to Exhale" soundtrack spun off three platinum (million-selling) singles -- Houston's "Exhale (Shoop Shoop)," Brandy's "Sittin' Up In My Room" and Mary J. Blige's "Not Gon' Cry." Houston's duet with gospel diva CeCe Winans, "Count On Me," went gold.

The other 7-million sellers were Smashing Pumpkins, who had the year's best-selling alternative rock album in "Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness," a double-disc set and the band's second multi-platinum title.
And the late rap singer Tupac Shakur, whose "All Eyez On Me" double-disc set racked up 7 million copies in sales en route to becoming the top rap album of all time, the RIAA said.
Other highlights of the year in music include Los Del Rio's "Macarena," which sold 4 million copies.

Overall the trade group said it counted 317 gold albums this year compared to 278 last year, and there were 23 new artists who achieved gold status or higher. The group handed out 158 platinum albums this year versus 191 in 1995.
The totals counted U.S. sales only.
